title: Intelligent driving intelligence test for autonomous vehicles with naturalistic and adversarial environment

control_signal.value: No user-facing signal. Designer supplies the AV under test (via surrogate models) and a criticality threshold; adversarial maneuvers are chosen automatically for the principal other vehicle at critical moments.

control_mechanism.value: Importance sampling: only the maneuver distribution of the principal other vehicle at critical moments is twisted using criticality (exposure frequency times RL-learned maneuver challenge); other vehicles keep naturalistic distributions.

base_model.value: Markov decision process model of naturalistic behavior from empirical maneuver distributions, with RL-learned maneuver challenge for car following and IDM/MOBIL surrogate models; run in CARLA and a highway traffic simulator.

datasets.value: Naturalistic driving data from the Safety Pilot Model Deployment and IVBSS programs (University of Michigan).

metrics.value: AV accident rate estimate, relative half-width (threshold 0.3) and number of tests needed, accident rate per type, simulation weight (likelihood ratio) and event diversity for adversarial examples.

controllability_evidence.value: To reach relative half-width 0.3, NADE needs 8.74 × 10^4 tests versus 4.39 × 10^7 in NDE (about 500 times faster) for AV-I, and 2.32 × 10^4 versus 1.41 × 10^8 (about 6,000 times) for AV-II.

stated_limitations.value: Needs large amounts of naturalistic driving data; case study simplified (highway, limited actions, vehicles only); no perception-related tests such as weather; surrogate model and AV prediction errors.

notes: Scenario/environment testing via importance sampling, not a learned generative model with user-facing control. The packet is plain text, so all passages carry the label 'pages 1'.
